items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: I met Arvell Shaw and Roy Burns and we went up to Stamford, Connecticut and rehearsed up there. And then I did the tour

ctx.x: That’s a good thing I think.

But anyway I went up and played for him. He asked me to play a couple of tunes and I played “Love for Sale,” and something else, something, I think “Yesterdays.” And he says okay, “You’ll be okay.” And then we had rehearsals. I met Arvell Shaw and Roy Burns and we went up to Stamford, Connecticut and rehearsed up there. And then I did the tour, I think I had to get permission from the school to take off and do the tour because although I wasn’t graduating, it would have some reflection on my grades. So I told…

on a regular basis. And then around 1960, February or March, Sarah Vaughan called. Her bass player, Richard Davis, had recommended me to her and I went out with her. And that was fantastic. That was the greatest experience I ever had musically up to that time. I learned more with Sarah Vaughan than I did in all the five years at Juilliard. But she has amassed so much information in her singing and by playing for her and hearing chords and the way she could, she passed that right on to me, just taught me the kind…
